nywaterway-special-njt-schedule.title: NY Waterway Special NJT Rail Customer Schedule
nywaterway-special-njt-schedule.note: The advisory and linked HNJTRailSch.jpg show an October 12–November 13 special Hoboken/NJT Terminal–Midtown W39th schedule, with separate Monday/Friday and Tuesday–Thursday morning/evening tables. The image marks some arrivals as drop-off only and has an apparent AM/PM typo in one Tuesday–Thursday morning cell. Individual departure times are not transcribed or independently verified.

cutover-dates.claim: NJ TRANSIT temporary Phase 2 schedules apply October 11–November 14, 2026. Regular schedules are expected November 15, subject to safety testing.

train-counts.claim: Phase 2 weekday train counts: M-B 64→60; M&E 148→139; NEC 133→113; NJCL 99→87; RVL 51→50.
train-counts.note: Briefing page 14. These are weekday line totals, not Sunday counts or a systemwide reduction percentage.

hoboken-diversion.claim: Weekday Midtown Direct M&E, Gladstone and Montclair-Boonton trains divert to Hoboken during Phase 2.

weekend-service.claim: Weekend Midtown Direct trains continue to PSNY, on adjusted schedules.

cross-honoring.claim: Eligible Midtown Direct Hoboken tickets/passes: PATH at Hoboken/33rd only; weekday NY Waterway Hoboken Terminal–W39th; NJ TRANSIT 126 to/from PABT, including Academy-operated 126 buses.
cross-honoring.note: See path-cross-honoring for designated gates and peak-direction restrictions; do not imply all PATH/ferry routes or all NJ TRANSIT tickets qualify.

single-track-operations.claim: Single-track operation between Newark and Secaucus during Phase 2.

rvl-one-seat-ride.claim: RVL one-seat PSNY trains originate/terminate at Newark Penn during the temporary schedule period.

path-travel-time.claim: PATH Hoboken to 33rd Street takes approximately 15 minutes
path-travel-time.note: Previously recorded estimate; current cutover timetable and observed journey times were not verified on October 11. Do not label as a guaranteed or current verified duration.

path-frequency.claim: Phase 2 weekday Hoboken–33rd PATH: every 6 minutes 7–9:30am and 4–7pm. Hoboken–WTC also receives 6-minute evening service.
path-frequency.note: Planned service, not live arrivals. Off-peak and Newark–WTC frequencies were not reverified.

ferry-travel-time.claim: NY Waterway ferry Hoboken to W. 39th St takes approximately 10–12 minutes
ferry-travel-time.note: Previously recorded estimate; current cutover timetable and observed journey times were not verified on October 11. Do not label as a guaranteed or current verified duration.

bus-126-travel-time.claim: Bus 126 from Hoboken to Port Authority takes 20–40 minutes depending on traffic
bus-126-travel-time.note: Previously recorded estimate; current cutover timetable and observed journey times were not verified on October 11. Do not label as a guaranteed or current verified duration.

bridge-age.claim: The Portal Bridge opened November 27, 1910 (115 years old as of 2026)

50-percent-reduction.claim: Approximately 50% service reduction between Newark and New York Penn Station
50-percent-reduction.note: Original evidence was February Phase 1. September 2026 secondary reports also describe roughly 50% fewer trains in the Newark–New York/Portal corridor, so this is not established as false or Phase 1-only. Current written primary sources checked do not establish the percentage; use the verified weekday line counts or clearly attribute a corridor-level news estimate. Do not generalize to systemwide cancellations.
50-percent-reduction.scope: Corridor-level percentage; not independently verified from current written primary sources

40000-man-hours.note: Briefing page 8; estimate, not completed work.

workers-per-shift.claim: Phase 2 staffing estimate: 50–75 workers per shift, two shifts daily, seven days per week.
workers-per-shift.note: Briefing page 8; replaces the Phase 1 staffing figure.

phase2-expected.claim: Final-track construction began October 9; NJ TRANSIT adjusted schedules start October 11, with regular schedules expected November 15 subject to safety testing.

gateway-program.claim: Portal North Bridge is part of the Gateway Program.

all-lines-affected.claim: All NJ TRANSIT rail lines except Atlantic City have temporary schedule adjustments.

flexpass.claim: FLEXPASS is on sale for Phase 2: 20 trips with a 15% discount.

presidents-day-schedule.claim: Feb 16 (Presidents' Day) runs holiday/weekend schedule; weekday Hoboken diversions begin Feb 17
presidents-day-schedule.note: Retained as historical metadata; not reverified October 11 and does not describe October 12, which uses the weekday cutover schedule. The mutable portal page now describes Phase 2.

fare-data.claim: NJT says eligible Midtown Direct riders buying Hoboken tickets and using cross-honored PATH/ferry can save up to 25% per trip, depending on origin.
fare-data.note: Exact station/zone dollar fares were not reverified and must not be presented as current verified fare data.

station-list-montclair-boonton.claim: 24 stations on Montclair-Boonton Line (10 Montclair branch, 14 Boonton branch)

station-list-morris-essex.claim: 28 stations on Morris & Essex Lines (16 Morristown, 12 Gladstone)

station-list-northeast-corridor.claim: 15 stations on Northeast Corridor (Trenton to Secaucus Junction)

station-list-north-jersey-coast.claim: 19 stations on North Jersey Coast Line (Bay Head to Avenel)

station-list-raritan-valley.claim: 16 stations on Raritan Valley Line (High Bridge to Union)

path-fare.note: Current TAPP Payments FAQ explicitly states a $3.25 one-way fare. Approved fare sheet retained as supporting background; no claim about exact May implementation date.

project-cost.claim: Portal North Bridge project cost approximately $1.8–2.3 billion
project-cost.note: Cost varies by source and what is included. FFGA amount is $1.73B; total project cost reported up to $2.3B

weekend-schedule-changes.claim: Weekend hourly timings may shift up to 30 minutes; Montclair remains bi-hourly with changed connections. Last Montclair/Gladstone connecting trips run 30 minutes earlier. Morristown–Hoboken connections move to Secaucus.
weekend-schedule-changes.note: Briefing page 15. Check individual temporary timetables.

weekend-ticket-validity.claim: Hoboken monthly/weekly passes and FLEXPASS are honored for weekend PSNY travel; one-way tickets must have a PSNY destination.

path-cross-honoring.claim: PATH accepts eligible Midtown Direct tickets at designated Hoboken turnstiles during morning peak and at 33rd Street in the peak travel direction. Newark and WTC are excluded.
path-cross-honoring.note: NJT describes station eligibility more generally. Follow PATH staff guidance outside the explicitly described peak-direction arrangements; all-day acceptance was not independently established.

october-12-schedule.claim: Monday October 12 uses NJ TRANSIT weekday cutover schedules; PATH operates regular weekday service with additional cutover trains.

brielle-replacement.claim: Buses replace Bay Head–Manasquan trains during Brielle work October 11–25.

brielle-accessibility.claim: Customers needing accessible boarding must board at Point Pleasant Beach; the bus continues to Asbury Park for train connections.

ferry-bus-connections.claim: NY Waterway publishes weekday peak routes on W34th/23rd, W42nd, W50th, W57th and a limited downtown route.
ferry-bus-connections.note: The September 13 map does not establish a Wall Street shuttle stop. Check current route-specific schedules.

ferry-service-window.claim: NY Waterway publishes a special weekday Hoboken/NJT Terminal–Midtown W39th ferry schedule for October 12–November 13, with separate Monday/Friday and Tuesday–Thursday morning and evening tables.
ferry-service-window.note: Verified the advisory publication date, effective window, terminals and weekday groupings against the linked schedule image. Consult the operator for individual trips and drop-off-only restrictions; an apparent AM/PM typo is not resolved here. This does not verify trip duration, fares, rail-ticket eligibility or real-time service.

verificationNote: Partial authoritative-source review on October 11, 2026, with a scoped ferry-schedule update on October 19. Per-claim dates and statuses control freshness; the top-level timestamp does not reverify every source or claim.
